formation.title: The Duchy Ascendant
formation.text:
The Mazovian lands are united under our banner, and Warsaw stands as the jewel of the Vistula. For generations, the Piast dukes of Mazovia have balanced between independence and vassalage, between the martial traditions of the petty nobility and the mercantile promise of the river trade. Now the duchy must choose its path. Shall we look inward to the legacy of the Piast bloodline, rallying our dense nobility to arms and asserting our ancient dynastic rights? Or shall we look outward along the Vistula, embracing Warsaw's potential as a great crossroads of commerce and learning?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are heirs of the Piasts: our blood is our strength.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Last Piasts
modifiers.text: The ducal house of Mazovia, last of the Piast line, draws upon centuries of dynastic memory to forge a realm defined by noble service and frontier defense.

options.text: The Vistula flows with gold: Warsaw shall be our gateway.

modifiers.name: Gate of the Vistula
modifiers.text: Warsaw commands the great river crossing where grain, timber, and amber flow from the interior to the Baltic, and the duchy means to profit from every barge that passes.

advances.name: Piast Strongholds
advances.text: The wooden fortified settlements along Mazovia's rivers, maintained since the earliest Piast dukes, form the backbone of frontier defense.

advances.name: Szlachta Horsemen
advances.text: Mazovia's petty nobility ride as light cavalry, not wealthy enough for heavy armor, but skilled horsemen who answer the ducal call in extraordinary numbers.

advances.name: Mazovian Rye Fields
advances.text: The lowland soils of Mazovia yield abundant harvests of rye, the staple grain that feeds the duchy and fuels its growing export trade.

advances.name: Ducal Court at Plock
advances.text: The Piast court at Plock administers the duchy with a blend of Polish custom and local Mazovian tradition.

advances.name: Parish Churches of Mazovia
advances.text: A network of stone and timber churches binds the Mazovian countryside together under the Catholic faith.

advances.name: Grunwald Banners
advances.text: The Mazovian knight contingent that fought at the Battle of Grunwald in 1410 cemented the duchy's martial reputation.

event.title: Under Mazovian Banners at Grunwald
event.text: In the summer of 1410, the Mazovian contingent marched alongside the forces of King Wladyslaw Jagiello against the Teutonic Order at Grunwald. Duke Siemowit of Mazovia led his knights into the greatest battle the region had ever seen, and the Teutonic state was broken. The Mazovian banners flew with honor that day, and the memory of this shared triumph has bound the duchy's nobility in martial pride ever since. Our knights proved that Mazovian valor stands equal to any in Christendom.

options.text: The honor of Grunwald lives in our banners.

modifiers.name: Grunwald Valor
modifiers.text: The memory of Mazovian banners flying at Grunwald inspires martial courage throughout the duchy.

advances.name: Czersk Castle
advances.text: The brick Gothic fortress at Czersk, raised by Duke Janusz I, is the architectural symbol of Mazovian ducal power.

advances.name: Warsaw: The New Capital
advances.text: Duke Janusz I's transfer of the ducal seat to Warsaw in 1413 marked the city's transformation from river crossing to political center.

event.title: Warsaw: The New Capital
event.text: Duke Janusz I has moved the ducal seat from Czersk to Warsaw, recognizing what the river crossing has become. Once a modest fishing village granted Magdeburg rights, Warsaw has grown into a thriving town of craftsmen, merchants, and petty nobles. The completion of St. John's Cathedral gave it spiritual gravity; the relocation of the ducal court gives it political authority. Granaries and wharves line the Vistula bank, and the new town spreads beyond the old walls. What was once peripheral has become central.

options.text: From this city, Mazovia shall prosper.

modifiers.name: Warsaw Ascendant
modifiers.text: The transfer of the ducal seat to Warsaw has accelerated the city's growth as a center of administration and learning.

advances.name: Vistula Granaries
advances.text: River-port warehouses at Warsaw and Plock store the duchy's grain for transport down the Vistula to Baltic markets.

event.title: The Granaries of the Vistula
event.text: Mazovian rye pours into the river warehouses at Warsaw and Plock, loaded onto flat-bottomed barges that ride the Vistula northward to the Baltic ports. The grain trade has transformed the duchy's economy, enriching the petty nobility who grow the crops and the burghers who handle the commerce. Every harvest now connects Mazovia to the wider world, the rye that grows in our fields feeds cities from Gdansk to Amsterdam.

advances.name: Dense Nobility
advances.text: Over twenty percent of Mazovia's population claims noble status, a uniquely dense gentry class that provides manpower beyond what the duchy's size would suggest. Most plough their own fields and ride to war as mounted crossbowmen.

advances.name: Magdeburg Charters
advances.text: The adoption of Magdeburg law grants Mazovian towns self-governance, codified legal rights, and structured market regulations.

advances.name: Pospolite Ruszenie
advances.text: The general levy of Mazovia's petty nobility, the pospolite ruszenie, musters a disproportionately large militia from the duchy's dense gentry class.

advances.name: Timber Rafting
advances.text: Mazovian timber is assembled into great rafts and floated down the Vistula to Gdansk, connecting the duchy's forests to the Baltic shipbuilding trade. The rafts are bound at the binduga, the timber yard on the river bank.

advances.name: Dozynki Tradition
advances.text: The harvest festivals of Mazovia bind lord and peasant in shared celebration, reinforcing social bonds and cultural continuity.

advances.name: Warsaw New Town
advances.text: The expansion of Warsaw beyond its medieval walls, with new suburbs for brewers, weavers, and artisans, signals the city's growing vitality.

advances.name: Crown Integration
advances.text: The incorporation of Mazovia into the Polish Crown following the extinction of the Piast male line in 1526 brings new administrative connections.

advances.name: Pancerni Cavalry Tradition
advances.text: The Mazovian pancerni, armored but agile cavalrymen, represent the evolution of the petty nobility's mounted traditions.

advances.name: Vistula Grain Fleet
advances.text: Organized convoys of river barges carry Mazovian grain to the Baltic, making the duchy a key link in Poland's grain export trade.

advances.name: Szlachta Privileges
advances.text: The golden liberties of the Polish-Lithuanian szlachta take particular root in Mazovia, where the petty nobility's numbers give them outsized political weight.

advances.name: Warsaw Sejm Sessions
advances.text: The holding of Sejm sessions in Warsaw cements the city's role as the de facto political capital of the Commonwealth.

advances.name: Agricultural Reforms
advances.text: Modernized farming techniques and estate management improve yields across the Mazovian lowlands.

advances.name: River Customs Houses
advances.text: Toll stations along the Vistula extract revenue from the endless stream of barges carrying grain, timber, and goods to the sea.

advances.name: Mazovian Resilience
advances.text: Through the upheavals of invasion and foreign domination, the Mazovian identity endures, stubborn, practical, and rooted in the land. In 1708 the Kurpie, hunters and bee keepers of the northern forest, fell on the Swedish king's column on the causeway at Kopanski Most.

advances.name: Warsaw Enlightenment
advances.text: The intellectual ferment of the Enlightenment reaches Warsaw, inspiring new schools, printing houses, and reform movements.

advances.name: Industrial Vistula
advances.text: Early manufactories spring up along the Vistula, harnessing river power and trade connections for the first stirrings of industrial production. The linen works founded for Philippe de Girard's flax spinning machines gives its name to a new town, Zyrardow.

advances.name: Mazovian National Identity
advances.text: In an era of empires and revolutions, the distinctive Mazovian character (its dialect, customs, and noble traditions) crystallizes into a conscious regional identity.

advances.name: Warsaw Urban Growth
advances.text: Warsaw's population swells as the city expands into a true metropolis, drawing migrants from across the region with its institutions and opportunities.

destiny.name: Mazovian Destiny
destiny.text: The duchy is formed and its future stretches before us. Mazovian destiny awaits those with the stability and vision to pursue it.

event.title: The Mazovian Destiny
event.text: Mazovia stands united and stable. The Piast banner flies over Warsaw and the duchy's future is ours to shape. Whether through the sword or through gold, Mazovia shall leave its mark on the world.

destiny.name: Piast Border March
destiny.text: The Teutonic frontier has long threatened Mazovia. Seize the Chelmno Land and Torun and raise ducal strongholds in three of our locations to establish a fortified border march under Piast authority.

conditions.text: Chose Legacy of the Last Piasts
A Ducal Grod stands in at least 3 of our locations

event.title: The Border March Secured
event.text: Mazovian banners now fly over Torun and the Chelmno Land. For generations the Teutonic Order harassed our northern frontier, demanding tribute and raiding our villages. No more. The border is secured, and the petty szlachta who rode to war return home as heroes. The duchy's martial reputation grows, and greater ambitions stir in the hearts of the Mazovian nobility.

destiny.name: Mazovian Crusade
destiny.text: With the border secured, the time has come to break the Teutonic state entirely. Take Marienburg, Elbing and Konigsberg to dismantle the Order's power.

event.title: The Teutonic State Broken
event.text: Marienburg has fallen. Konigsberg submits. The once-fearsome Teutonic Order, which terrorized our ancestors for centuries, lies broken beneath Mazovian arms. The grand castles of the Order now serve Mazovian purposes, and the wealth of Prussia's amber coast flows into our treasury. How shall we consolidate this hard-won conquest?

options.text: Strip the Order's castles for our defense.

modifiers.name: Teutonic Spoils
modifiers.text: The captured fortifications and armories of the Teutonic Order have been repurposed for Mazovian defense.

options.text: Rally every noble who can ride to our cause.

modifiers.name: Szlachta Banners Unfurled
modifiers.text: Every petty noble in Mazovia answers the call to arms, swelling our ranks but straining the treasury.

destiny.name: Shield of the Piasts
destiny.text: The Piast dynasty stands as the shield of Christendom's northern frontier. Hold Memel and reach Riga to command the entire eastern Baltic coast and cement Mazovian military supremacy.

event.title: Shield of the Piasts
event.text: From Warsaw to Riga, the eastern Baltic bows to Mazovian power. What began as a modest duchy on the Vistula has become a military state stretching across the northern plains. The Piast dynasty, last of its ancient line, has forged an empire through discipline and the courage of its dense szlachta cavalry. How shall history remember this achievement?

options.text: As conquerors who dictated terms to kings.

modifiers.name: Piast Hegemony
modifiers.text: The Piast dynasty dictates terms to its neighbors from a position of unassailable military strength.

options.text: As the bulwark that held the northern frontier.

modifiers.name: Frontier Bulwark
modifiers.text: Mazovia stands as an immovable bulwark on the northern frontier, drawing mercenaries and supplies from across the realm.

destiny.name: Baltic Outlet
destiny.text: Mazovian grain flows down the Vistula but others profit at the river's mouth. Take Gdansk to control the Baltic outlet and keep the wealth in Mazovian hands.

event.title: The Baltic Outlet Secured
event.text: Gdansk is ours. The great port at the mouth of the Vistula, where Mazovian grain and timber have always been destined, now flies the Piast banner. No longer do foreign merchants set the terms of trade for our harvest. The barges that depart Warsaw arrive at our own docks, and the wealth that once enriched Hanseatic strangers now fills Mazovian coffers.

options.text: The river's wealth flows to us at last.

destiny.name: Vistula Commerce
destiny.text: With the Baltic outlet secured, develop Warsaw into a major commercial center. Build up the city, draw amber into the capital market, and build a trade empire along the river.

conditions.text: We own Warsaw and its development is at least 32

children.text: Amber is produced in the market
Amber is traded in the market

event.title: Masters of the Vistula Trade
event.text: Warsaw's markets hum with commerce. Amber and grain flow through our capital, bankers extend credit to merchants across the region, and the Vistula has become the most profitable trade artery in Central Europe. Our commercial influence extends far beyond what the duchy's modest size would suggest. How shall we leverage this position?

options.text: Our grain feeds nations: let diplomacy follow.

modifiers.name: Grain Fortune
modifiers.text: The wealth generated by the Vistula grain trade opens diplomatic doors and funds intelligence networks across Europe.

options.text: Draw all roads to Warsaw through trade and treaty.

modifiers.name: Amber Road
modifiers.text: Control of the amber trade routes draws foreign merchants and vassals into Warsaw's commercial orbit.

destiny.name: Crown of the Vistula
destiny.text: Command the entire length of the Vistula from Krakow to Gdansk. Grow Warsaw into a city or the center of its own market, and amass the wealth to make it the undisputed center of Central European commerce.

conditions.text: We own Warsaw and it is a city or the center of a market

event.title: Crown of the Vistula
event.text: From Krakow's salt mines to Gdansk's harbor, the entire Vistula corridor answers to Mazovian commerce. What other nations achieved through conquest, we built through counting houses and markets. Warsaw stands as a great emporium of Central Europe, where merchants from the Baltic to the Black Sea come to do business. The Piast banner has become a symbol not of war, but of prosperity.

options.text: Warsaw shall be the emporium of the North.

modifiers.name: Warsaw Emporium
modifiers.text: Warsaw's status as a great trade center projects diplomatic influence, though maintaining the commercial infrastructure diverts resources from the military.

options.text: We shall lead a league of Vistula cities.

modifiers.name: Vistula League
modifiers.text: A confederation of Vistula trading cities under Mazovian leadership expands our diplomatic reach, though the cities bargain their taxes down in return.

units.name: Mazovian Szlachta Cavalry
units.text: Light horsemen drawn from Mazovia's dense petty nobility, not heavily armored, but numerous and skilled riders who answer the ducal call in extraordinary numbers.

units.name: Zagrodowa Horse
units.text: Yeoman gentry who plough their own fields. Too poor for a lance and harness, they ride as mounted crossbowmen, lightly protected and very many.

units.name: Mazovian Rycerz
units.text: Armored Piast knights who proved their valor at Grunwald, these heavy cavalrymen are the martial elite of the Mazovian duchy.

units.name: Pospolite Militia
units.text: The general levy of Mazovia's petty nobility, tough defenders who fight for their own farms and families, requiring little supply from the ducal treasury.

units.name: Mazovian Pancerni
units.text: Medium-armored cavalry drawn from the Mazovian szlachta, versatile horsemen who bridge the gap between light raiders and heavy lancers.

units.name: Kurpie Marksmen
units.text: Hunters and bee keepers of the Green Forest on the Narew. Deadly from cover among the trees, without drill or bayonets in the open.

buildings.name: Ducal Grod
buildings.text: A fortified timber settlement of the Piast tradition, combining garrison, granary, and administrative center along Mazovia's rivers.

buildings.name: Vistula Wharf
buildings.text: A riverside warehouse and landing where grain, timber, and goods are loaded onto barges for transport down the Vistula.

buildings.name: Binduga
buildings.text: The timber yard on the river bank, where logs hauled from the forest are sorted and bound into rafts for the float to Gdansk.

where.text: Lumber is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Mazovian Kancelaria
buildings.text: The ducal chancellery, where Magdeburg law is administered and the affairs of the duchy are recorded in increasingly systematic fashion.

buildings.name: Vistula Toll Station
buildings.text: A customs post on the riverbank where toll collectors extract duties from every barge passing through Mazovian waters.

buildings.name: Szlachta Manor
buildings.text: The modest country estate of a Mazovian petty noble, more farm than palace, but the backbone of the duchy's manpower.

buildings.name: Warsaw Printing House
buildings.text: A center of Enlightenment publishing, producing books, pamphlets, and newspapers that spread new ideas across Mazovia.

buildings.name: Zyrardow Linen Works
buildings.text: A spinning works built around Philippe de Girard's flax machines. The linen is sold bleached, and the settlement beside the works bears his name.

where.text: Fiber Crops is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Mazovian Arsenal
buildings.text: A centralized weapons depot and armory supplying the Piast military machine with arms, armor, and siege equipment.

buildings.name: Vistula Kontora
buildings.text: A grand counting house and trade exchange where merchants negotiate the terms of Vistula commerce under Mazovian law.

list.name: Statuty Mazowieckie
list.text: The criminal-procedural code Duke Siemowit III promulgated at Sochaczew on 27 April 1377 and revised in 1390. The statutes regulated wergeld for the killing of a wlodyka or well-to-do peasant, defined the conditions of lawful feud, and bound the ducal courts to written procedure. Mazovia's adoption of statute law half a century before the Crown's own systematic codifications gave Siemowit's cadet duchy a juridical authority disproportionate to its territory, and made the Sochaczew text a referent for Mazovian land courts long after incorporation into the Polish Crown in 1526.

list.name: Sejmiki of Czersk and Warsaw
list.text: The Mazovian noble assemblies that ratified the duchy's first general land privilege at Nowe Miasto on 21 June 1414, granted jointly to the szlachta of the Czersk and Warsaw districts by Janusz I. The sejmiki retained the right to consent to extraordinary taxation and military levy, codifying a consultative custom that survived incorporation into the Crown in 1526 and later furnished the Mazovian voivodeships with their distinctive pre-sejm position in Polish constitutional life.

list.name: Ksiegi Ziemskie Mazowieckie
list.text: The land-court record series the Mazovian dukes mandated kept district by district from the second decade of the fifteenth century, with separate volumes opened at Rozan in 1412, Makow in 1413, and the Czersk and Warsaw districts from 1414 onward. The ksiegi recorded inheritances, land sales, mortgages, and dowries in registers successors and creditors could consult at the regional court; for the szlachta and the Vistula towns alike, the written rolls transformed property from oral memory into legally binding title.

list.name: Plock Cathedral Chapter
list.text: The canonical college serving the Cathedral of the Assumption at Plock, organised under Wladyslaw Herman from the Benedictine community of Saint Laurentius and raised to a fully constituted chapter under metropolitan Gniezno. By Conrad of Mazovia's 1239 charter the chapter co-administered some 240 villae and twenty praedia of episcopal land; the canons supplied the duchy's literate chancery clerks, kept the bishopric archive, and crowned eight of the early Piast princes in the cathedral nave where they were also entombed alongside the dukes of Mazovia.

list.name: Ducal Chancery of Warsaw
list.text: The Piast chancery Janusz I removed from Czersk Castle to Warsaw on assuming sole rule of the eastern duchy in 1413, and from which he issued the great corpus of Mazovian privileges from 1414 onward. The chancery employed cathedral-trained notaries from the Plock chapter, maintained the ducal seal, drafted mandates and confirmations, and supplied the legal staff who opened the district court books across Mazovia. After incorporation in 1526 its personnel furnished the new Mazovian voivodeship without interruption of administrative routine.
